privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: We built this service to collect as little as possible. This page explains exactly what we handle, why, and what you can do about it.

sections.h: QR codes are made in your browser
p: When you create a QR code without an account, everything happens on your device: the link, WiFi password, contact details or text you type, and any logo you add, are never sent to our servers.
Downloads (PNG, SVG, PDF) are generated on your device too. We do not store the QR codes you create this way.

An account is only needed for the business card, the link-in-bio page and their statistics. You sign in with Google. Google shares your name, email address and profile picture with us; we never see your Google password.
We use this information only to run your account. Account data is stored by our backend provider, InsForge, in the United States.

We use only what the site needs to work: two sign-in cookies (insforge_access_token, insforge_refresh_token), a short-lived cookie used during Google sign-in (insforge_code_verifier, 10 minutes), a cookie that remembers your language (NEXT_LOCALE), and a local-storage entry that remembers your cookie choice.
We do not use advertising cookies, third-party trackers or session-recording tools. Our fonts are served from our own site, not from Google.

To know which pages are useful, our own servers record anonymous events: the page viewed, the language, QR downloads (type and format only, never the content), the type of device, the country estimated from the connection and the site you came from. We do not store your IP address, we never record what you type, and no outside analytics company receives this data.
If you click Accept on the cookie banner, a random identifier kept only for the current browser tab is added, so we can count unique visitors. If you choose Essential only, no identifier is used.

sections.h: Business cards, link pages and payments
p: The information you put on a business card or link page (name, logo, photos, hours, address, phone, links) is published on a public page, because that is its purpose.
Payments are handled by Stripe. Your card number goes directly to Stripe and never passes through our servers.
When a subscription ends, the page is suspended for 30 days so you can come back, then deleted.
For business cards and link pages, we count visits, QR scans and taps on buttons, per day. We do not build profiles of the people who visit, and we never sell this data.
InsForge (database, sign-in, file storage), Vercel (website hosting), Google (sign-in) and Stripe (payments). Each acts on our instructions and only for the service it provides.
We do not sell or rent personal information, and we do not share it for advertising. This includes the meaning of sale and sharing under the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA).

You can ask to see the personal information we hold about you, to correct it, or to delete your account and everything linked to it. California residents have these rights under the CCPA; we offer them to everyone. Write to us at the address below and we will answer within 30 days.

Accounts are for adults only: you must be 18 or older to sign in. The free generator needs no account and collects no personal information. We do not knowingly collect information from anyone under 18; if you think a minor has an account, tell us and we will delete it.
If we change how we handle data, we will update this page and the date at the top before the change applies.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: These terms apply when you use the QR code generator, the hosted business card and the link-in-bio page.

p: The free generator is open to everyone. Creating an account, a business card or a link page is reserved for people aged 18 or older. By signing in you confirm that you are at least 18 and accept these terms and the privacy policy.
You can create and download QR codes for free, without an account and without a watermark.
QR codes for links, WiFi, text, vCards, email and SMS are static: the information is inside the code itself, so they keep working forever and do not depend on our service.
You keep all rights to what you upload (logos, photos, texts). You give us a limited licence to store, display and reproduce it only to run your card or page and show it to visitors.

You must own your content or have permission to use it. Do not upload images, logos or texts that belong to someone else. You are responsible for what you publish and for the sites your QR codes point to.
If we receive a valid copyright notice, we remove or disable the content concerned, as described in our copyright policy. Accounts that repeatedly infringe are closed.

Do not use the service for phishing, malware, scams, illegal content, harassment, copyright infringement, or to impersonate someone else. Every public page has a Report button; we may hide or remove content that breaks these rules, and suspend the account behind it.
The business card and the link page are each a paid subscription, monthly or yearly, at the price shown next to the subscribe button at the time you subscribe, plus any applicable taxes.

The subscription renews automatically at the end of each period (every month or every year) and you are charged the same price with the payment method on file, until you cancel. Before you pay, we show these terms and ask you to agree to them.
You can cancel at any time, online, with the Manage billing button in your dashboard. Cancellation stops the next renewal; your page stays online until the end of the period already paid.
If we ever change the price, we tell you before your next renewal and the new price applies only after it.
Payments are not refundable, including for unused time after you cancel, except where the law of your country requires a refund. You keep full access until the end of the period you paid for.

If a payment fails or a subscription ends, the page is suspended for 30 days and is then deleted with its images. Your page's address (its slug) never changes, so printed QR codes keep pointing to the right place while the page exists.
We work to keep the service online but cannot promise it will always be available or error-free. Static QR codes you downloaded are not affected by any outage.
The service is provided as is. To the extent the law allows, we are not liable for indirect losses, or for losses caused by content you or others publish.
We may update these terms. We will change the date at the top, and for important changes we will tell account holders by email before they apply.

copyright.title: Copyright policy
copyright.intro: We respect intellectual property and expect our users to do the same. Here is how to report content that infringes your copyright, and how we handle it (Digital Millennium Copyright Act, DMCA).

p: If you believe a business card or link page hosted on our service uses your work without permission, send a written notice to our designated agent at the contact address below. You can also use the Report button on the page and choose Copyright, then send the full notice by email.

1) Your physical or electronic signature. 2) The work you say is infringed. 3) The address (URL) of the page and a description of the content to remove. 4) Your name, postal address, telephone number and email. 5) A statement that you believe in good faith that the use is not authorised by the owner, its agent or the law. 6) A statement, under penalty of perjury, that the information is accurate and that you are the owner or authorised to act for them.
Incomplete notices may not be acted on. Knowingly false notices can make you liable for damages.
When we receive a valid notice, we promptly remove or disable access to the content and tell the account holder, with a copy of the notice.

If your content was removed by mistake, you can send a counter-notice with: your signature; the content removed and where it appeared; a statement under penalty of perjury that you believe in good faith it was removed by mistake; your name, address and telephone number; and your consent to the jurisdiction of the federal court for your district (or, outside the United States, any district where we may be found) and to accept service from the person who sent the notice.
We forward it to that person and may restore the content after 10 to 14 business days unless they tell us they have filed a court action.
We close the accounts of users who repeatedly infringe the rights of others.
Our designated agent for copyright notices is the operator of this site, at the postal and email address shown below.

faq.q: Is this QR code generator really free?
faq.a: Yes. Static QR codes are free forever, with no sign-up, no watermark and no scan limit. You can use them commercially.
No. Static QR codes encode your content directly, so they keep working forever, even if you never create an account.

faq.q: Can I add a logo to my QR code?
faq.a: Yes. Upload your logo, pick colors, dot and corner styles, and add a frame with a call to action like "Scan me".
PNG for web and social, SVG vector for print at any size, and PDF ready for printing.

faq.q: What can a QR code link to?
faq.a: A website URL, WiFi network, vCard contact, email, SMS, phone number, PDF, WhatsApp, Instagram, Google Maps and many more.

faq.q: What is the difference between static and dynamic QR codes?
faq.a: A static QR code stores the data inside the pattern and can't be edited. A dynamic QR code points to a short link you can change later and track scans.
